title: Cyprian (d. 258)
hook: you can't have God for your father without the Church for your mother; and the fight over welcoming back the lapsed

segments.voice: Yesterday, Origen and Alexandria. Your line was layers of meaning. Did the psalm line say something new the second time? Day seven hundred twelve.

The persecution is over, and the church in Carthage has a problem nobody prepared for. During it, an emperor's order told everyone to sacrifice to the gods. Some Christians refused, and suffered for it. Some ran. And some gave in: they burned the incense, or bought a certificate saying they had. Now the danger has passed, and those who gave in are standing at the church door, asking to come home. The bishop, Cyprian, has to answer them. So does everyone else.
screen: `THE PERSECUTION IS OVER.` → `SOME GAVE IN.` → `NOW THEY'RE AT THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: First, Cyprian's own position was awkward. When the persecution began, he went into hiding and led his people by letters. He said it was for their sake. Some said he'd run. So when he speaks about those who fell, he isn't speaking from a pedestal. The church called them the lapsed, the fallen. Second, two loud answers. Some of the confessors, Christians who had suffered and survived, began writing notes of peace, welcoming the lapsed back at once, no questions asked. At Rome, a priest named Novatian took the opposite line: those who had denied Christ could never be taken back by the Church. Third, Cyprian's way. Not at once, and not never. In his book On the Lapsed, he grieves over them. He asks for real repentance, time, and a decision by the bishops together, not a quick pardon from one person. And then, a welcome home. Fourth, the picture behind it all. In another book, On the Unity of the Church, he writes the line on today's screen, put simply: no one can have God for his Father who doesn't have the Church for his mother. A mother can be strict. A mother also keeps the door open and sets a place at the table. For Cyprian, that was the Church: one family, holding the line and holding out its arms. He died a martyr in the end. The account says that when the sentence was read, he answered: thanks be to God.
screen: `SOME GAVE IN.` · `AT ONCE, OR NEVER?` · `REPENTANCE, THEN HOME.` · `GOD FATHER, CHURCH MOTHER.` · then, large: `THE CHURCH IS MOTHER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: welcome someone back. Settle, and breathe. Think of someone who drifted away: from your family, your friends, your parish, or from you. Maybe they let you down. Maybe it just faded. Hold their face for a moment, honestly, the hurt included if there is some. Then ask what a first step back toward them would look like. Not pretending nothing happened. Just an open door. A message, a wave, an invitation. If you pray, you can hold them before God. The bell holds the time.
Cyprian. The bishop of Carthage who called the lapsed home through repentance, and said the Church is our mother. Today's word.
Your line: the Church is mother. Today, take the first small step toward the person you thought of. Day seven hundred twelve.

howItsDone: Catholics remember Saint Cyprian together with Pope Saint Cornelius in the Church's calendar, and both are named in the Roman Canon; the sacrament of penance is the Church's ordinary way of welcoming back those who have fallen.

fork.setup: you're a bishop. Christians who gave in under persecution want to come back. some say take them at once; some say never. what do you do?
options: take them back at once, no questions.
fork.reveal: Cyprian chose neither extreme: real repentance, a decision by the bishops together, and then a welcome home.

original.note: Latin: the lapsed, the fallen — the name for Christians who gave in under persecution.

trapdoor: what you thought: the early Church was all heroes and martyrs.
what it means: some gave in, and Cyprian had to decide how to bring them home.
what a scholar hears: On the Lapsed and On the Unity of the Church, written amid a dispute over readmitting the fallen, with Novatian at Rome.

notes: On the Unity of the Church 6 paraphrased ('no one can have God for his Father who doesn't have the Church for his mother'), not quoted, since the public-domain wording isn't verified here.
The persecution is left unnamed ('an emperor's order'); it is the persecution under Decius. Sacrifice, incense and bought certificates (libelli) as forms of lapsing: confirm.

Cyprian's withdrawal into hiding and the criticism of it; confessors' letters of peace; insistence on penance and a common decision of bishops; Novatian's rigorist position at Rome: confirm the summary, especially that Novatian was 'a priest' at the time.
Acts of Cyprian: his answer 'Deo gratias' to the sentence, rendered 'thanks be to God'. Confirm.
Feast shared with Cornelius and both names in the Roman Canon: confirm.

Editor: 'the ones who slipped' (a word-picture for lapsi) to plain 'the fallen' in teach and original note; 'grieves over them like a father' cut to 'grieves over them' (On the Lapsed 4 has him grieve with them, and the father image clashed with the mother picture the day builds to).

Audit (y3 auditor): checked; no voice change. Keeper may note that Cyprian's line was tiered (certificate-buyers readmitted after penance sooner than those who sacrificed, whom the African council of 251 at first reconciled only at death, relaxed in 252); the script's 'repentance, time, then a welcome home' is a fair simplification.
